articles.title: Houseplant hacks: should you always quarantine new plants to avoid pests spreading?
articles.summary: Any new addition to your collection can contain stowaways, so you’d be wise to deploy a little patience – but how long is long enough? The problem There is nothing quite like the joy of bringing home a new plant.
body: The hack Quarantining means keeping any new plant separated from the rest of your collection for a few weeks before letting it join the others. The logic is simple: if something is going to emerge, you want it to do so in isolation, where it can be dealt with before it spreads to the whole crew.

The method Place your new plant in a different room from the rest of your collection for two or three weeks. Every few days, check for webbing, sticky residue, tiny moving specks, or gnats rising from the compost. Treat any pests while the plant is isolated, and only move it in with the others once you are confident it is clean.

The test I have been quarantining new plants for several years now, and it works. New arrivals have come in with the odd stowaway, but because they were isolated, whatever they brought stayed contained to that one pot rather than becoming everyone’s problem.

The verdict Nearly every serious infestation I have seen, my own included, traces back to a new plant being introduced straight into your home collection. Quarantining is not a sign of paranoia; it’s the best way to protect your plants, and it costs nothing but a little patience.

articles.title: Transylvania beyond the spooky castles: a family adventure in Romania’s mountains
articles.summary: Forget the vampire tales – the Eastern Carpathians deliver dramatic peaks, roaming bears and deep solitude. As the sun disappears behind the high tree line, our campfire spits and crackles.
body: “This area is very wild,” says Samir Teslovan, who drove us up through the densely forested peaks from his guesthouse in Toplița. “When I come here to the mountains, I charge my battery, charge my soul. I feel free, like the wind.”

Sitting on the edge of a fragrant forest of spruce, fir, beech and pine, our view stretches over the valley to misty mountains receding in layers to the horizon. Samir points to a far-off peak in the east, a pyramid on a ragged ridge. “That’s Ukraine, maybe 200km,” he tells us. Then, pointing west: “That way, 400km, is Hungary.” The forest is still home to bears, wolves and lynx, but it’s the solitude that brings him here. “I prefer wild zones, where no one goes,” he says. “There are places here that nobody knows.”

Across the vast forests and mountains of Harghita County in central Romania, there are many places that nobody knows. In fact, the whole region has flown under the radar of international travellers – 85% of visitors come from Romania itself, which feels bizarre when you discover the wonders here, as we did on a 12-day family road trip, staying at self-catering lodges and cabins along the way.

articles.title: Student bank accounts: don’t be swayed by the freebies, freshers told
articles.summary: Sign-up perks may capture the attention but should the focus be on the interest-free overdraft? The best student deals and discounts. An insider’s tips on student money.
body: I n the scramble to sort out university accommodation, join freshers group chats and work out how a student loan payment is meant to stretch across a whole term, there is one big decision that is easy to put off but worth getting right: which student bank account to open.

Student accounts work like any other current account but come with two extras that don’t apply to the general public: an interest-free overdraft, and a lot of perks designed to hook you in as a customer for life.
However, while it is tempting to choose an account on the strength of the free cash, vouchers or other goodies, personal finance experts advise you not to be swayed by the extras.
“An interest-free overdraft could provide greater value over the course of a degree than a one-off freebie,” says Caitlyn Eastell at Moneyfactscompare.co.uk.

articles.title: Inside Jordyn Woods and Karl-Anthony Towns’ Classic Wedding Weekend in Malibu
articles.summary: After six years together, the model-entrepreneur and New York Knicks star exchanged vows at a private estate overlooking the Pacific, with custom Danielle Frankel for the bride and Ralph Lauren for the groom.
body: On Saturday, August 15, model and entrepreneur Jordyn Woods and New York Knicks center and NBA Champion Karl-Anthony Towns married surrounded by family and friends at a private home overlooking the ocean in Malibu.

The couple first met nine years ago in Los Angeles in 2017, where Karl was spending his off-season and where Jordyn grew up. “We connected over a game of Uno, and he thinks that he won,” Jordyn remembers. “We both have a very competitive nature. When we play games, we are not on the same team—we are in it to win.”

The two became close and were good friends for two years before they eventually started dating in 2020. “I lost my dad at 19,” Jordyn says. “And during Covid, his mom got sick and passed, and I was able to be there for him in a different way.”

articles.title: How to Style Wide-Leg Jeans, According to the Street-Style Set
articles.summary: Wide-leg jeans are one of the most popular denim trends, and this is how to style yours, with inspiration straight from the street style set.
body: Over the past few years, denim trends have been a particularly hot topic here at Vogue HQ. From the divisive barrel leg and ultra-low-rise styles, to the return of skinny jeans, there has been no shortage of denim shapes to debate—and, in many cases, internet discourses to fuel. For 2026, however, the denim styles leading the conversation feel, by comparison, reassuringly familiar.

“Straight-leg and high-waisted cuts from the spring/summer 2026 collections didn’t stray far from classic shapes, with enduring qualities that exist beyond the seasonal trend cycle,” Vogue ’s Alice Cary noted in her guide to this year’s denim styles, spotlighting failsafe fits like the classic straight-leg, cropped and slightly wide-leg as standouts for 2026.

articles.title: A Bad Bunny and a Beagle Walk Into a Restaurant…
articles.summary: After wrapping his eight-month-long Debí Tirar Más Fotos World Tour, Bad Bunny had one thing left to do: an Italian dinner date with his beagle, Sansa.
body: After wrapping his eight-month-long Debí Tirar Más Fotos World Tour at the end of July, Bad Bunny had one thing left to do before a well-deserved vacation: an Italian dinner date with a very special lady. So mere days after he took his final bow in Brussels, the singer—also known as Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio—strolled into a restaurant in his native Puerto Rico with Sansa Martínez Berlingeri, his four-year-old beagle.

The singer got Sansa when she was just three months old. Her personality, which he describes as affectionate, playful, and sometimes “ un poco bicha —but nice,” earned the young pup her Game of Thrones –inspired name. “She has that same strength and presence,” Martínez Ocasio says of the similarities between the pup and Sophie Turner’s character, Sansa Stark. “The name just felt right from the beginning.”

articles.title: You Can Now Use Whoop's Blood Tests Without a Membership
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Whoop, the company best known for its screen-free fitness band, continues to expand its domain in the broader healthcare space.
body: Since Whoop launched Advanced Labs last fall, you needed a Whoop membership in order to connect your blood test results with the company's continuous health monitoring in the Whoop app. Now the lab testing stands on its own as a direct-to-consumer product—continuing the trend of companies like Whoop wanting to grow beyond "wearables" into comprehensive, one-stop-shop health platforms.

The newly added Galleri test works a bit differently. It's a single blood draw that screens for a signal shared across more than 50 cancer types, many of which have no standard screening protocol today. To be clear, it detects a signal suggesting cancer may be present, not a diagnosis, and it's meant to supplement the screenings your doctor already recommends, not replace them. Advanced Labs isn't currently covered by insurance, though purchases may qualify for HSA or FSA reimbursement, which you should confirm with your plan administrator before you buy.
